solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fortunate I am on horse: no fun here on bike?

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the fortunate part follows the horse

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
blest is a poetic form of blessed, fortunate
one's is short for one is, which is a formal way of saying I am

explanation.surface: A lucky rider declares themselves happy on horseback, since riding a bicycle somewhere is no fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a cryptic definition: cobbled streets make for a bone-shaking bike ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounded stones paving old streets give cyclists a jarring, unpleasant ride, hence no fun on a bike.

clue.text: Girl in school stuck with another

indicators.note: in places the girl within the school word

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school
her stands for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl at school is joined to a classmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohered means held together or stuck to something else.

clue.text: Having burned oneself very badly, an anxious case

indicators.note: badly means in a damaged way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has scalded themselves severely is now a nervous wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A bundle of nerves is an idiom for a very anxious, jittery person.

clue.text: Neglect to send out Times: they haven't taken orders

indicators.note: to send out is to expel, so the times sign leaves the word

parts.note: laxity is slackness or neglect
X is the multiplication or times sign

explanation.surface: Someone forgets to post the newspaper, and the staff haven't taken instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken orders' means been ordained: the laity are those who are not clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are ordinary churchgoers, not ordained clergy who have taken holy orders.

clue.text: House not ever needed as college

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
nary is a dialect word meaning not a single or never

explanation.surface: A residence that was never required serves as a college.
explanation.walkthrough: A SEMI is a British semi-detached house, one sharing a wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college for training priests or ministers.

clue.text: Female avoiding wife's state

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so the wife letter is removed

parts.note: a woman is a female
W is the abbreviation for wife; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A woman shuns a married woman's country.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a sovereign country on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Do they spread the cost of a superficial education?

definitions.text: Do they spread the cost of a superficial education?

parts.words: Do they spread the cost of a superficial education?
parts.note: a payment plan spreads costs; read differently, a few undemanding school sessions make a light education

explanation.surface: A question about financing a shallow schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: Terms are also school terms, so easy ones suggest a superficial education.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy terms are instalment arrangements that spread the cost of a purchase over time.

clue.text: Shy contender, he turned out founder of a dynasty

indicators.note: turned out means rearranged into a new shape

explanation.surface: A timid rival proves to have founded a royal line.
explanation.definitionFit: This king founded the Plantagenet (Angevin) royal line that ruled England for centuries.

clue.text: You being laid in earth was excessively sickening

indicators.note: being laid in means put down inside, so you goes into the earth

parts.note: a clod is a lump of earth
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A burial in the ground proved deeply nauseating.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloyed means became too sweet or rich to bear, surfeiting and sickening.

clue.text: Chinese switch positions in capital

parts.note: the Han are the majority ethnic group of China
electrical switches mark their on and off positions with the symbols I and O

explanation.surface: A Chinese person moves to a different role within a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Switch positions are the I and O printed on power switches, not an instruction to rearrange letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Grasping toff has a heart of gold?

parts.note: grasping means stingy, mean with money
a swell is an old-fashioned word for a fashionable upper-class man, a toff

explanation.surface: A greedy posh person turns out to be kind-hearted after all.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for an upper-class person. The stingy toff of the surface is a contradiction of the definition, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who means well has good intentions, which is roughly having a kind heart.

clue.text: Driving competitively, squeezing teammate into roundabout, perhaps

indicators.note: squeezing one thing into another puts it inside, so the teammate goes within
into names the piece that receives the squeezed-in teammate

parts.note: a roundabout is circular, an example of a ring
an ally is someone on your side, a teammate

explanation.surface: A reckless driver forces a fellow team member off into a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundabout, perhaps' defines by example: a roundabout is one kind of ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallying is motor sport on roads or tracks, a form of competitive driving.

clue.text: Firm resistance: read all about it

indicators.note: all about means wholly surrounding, so the word for read goes round the resistance, the it of the clue

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A determined opponent echoes the newspaper seller's call to read all about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read all about it' is the newsboy's cry; here 'it' points back to the resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy and firm are synonyms describing something solid and strongly built.

clue.text: Your extremely evil master's twisted jesting

indicators.note: twisted here means turned right round, so the assembled letters read backwards
extremely asks for the extreme letters, first and last, of each word

parts.note: a lord is a master; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone's cruel boss has a perverse sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' looks like an anagram signal but is a reversal: YR, EL and LORD together read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is comic, whimsical humour, the same thing as jesting.

clue.text: Rock and roll single gripping me

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside, so the roll word holds the me

parts.note: a list is a roll, as in a register of names
taken as written
one is a single

explanation.surface: A rock and roll single grabs the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock and roll' is split: Rock is the definition, roll is LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone is a sedimentary rock made mostly of calcium carbonate.

clue.text: To be ranked worse than F went down badly

parts.note: in letter grading G comes after F, so it ranks lower
rated means ranked or graded

explanation.surface: Being given a grade below F was poorly received.
explanation.walkthrough: G-RATED is also a film certificate, lending the surface extra cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that grated irritated people, so it was received badly.

clue.text: Composer's astonishing feat, in captivating monarch

indicators.note: captivating means capturing and holding, so the monarch is held within

parts.note: a coup is a brilliant, surprising success
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a monarch

explanation.surface: A composer's amazing achievement lies in charming the king.
explanation.definitionFit: François Couperin was a French Baroque composer and harpsichordist.

clue.text: Perhaps designer garments last for one season — gets darker clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the darkening word dresses round the picked letters

parts.note: dims means grows darker

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of each of the words one and season

explanation.surface: A fashion line of designer clothes lasts one season before darker garments take over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as a noun but is the verb: the darkening word dresses round the final letters of one and season.
explanation.definitionFit: Denims are jeans and other denim clothing, often sold as designer labels.

clue.text: Prosecutor not to reveal being a silk

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor
to mask is to hide, not to reveal

explanation.surface: A prosecutor refuses to disclose being a senior barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: A silk is a British senior barrister (King's Counsel), which steers away from the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric, often silk.

clue.text: Won't share: had to drink initially enormous amount of alcohol

parts.note: someone who hogs something keeps it all to themselves

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so the word had swallows the letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word enormous

explanation.surface: A greedy drinker who refuses to share has downed a huge quantity of booze.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask, and a measure of beer or wine of roughly fifty gallons.

clue.text: Period of relaxation having taking a knock largely with alien invasion

indicators.note: an invasion is a force entering, so the alien goes inside
largely means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: dented means having taken a knock
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A spell of rest is interrupted by an extra-terrestrial invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Detente is an easing of tension, especially between rival nations.

clue.text: Memory returning, fool is in confused state

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the memory abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: As someone's memory comes back, a foolish person finds themselves bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is literally a bog, figuratively a muddled, entangling situation.

clue.text: Frenchman's duck, caught by a favourite opener

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so the French nothing sits within the other pieces

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
a duck is a zero score in cricket; rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: A French man's duck dinner is pounced on by a beloved starter dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of nothing; 'opener' suggests a cricket batsman but means a laxative, something that opens the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperient is a mild laxative, a medicine that opens the bowels.

clue.text: I hear you pulled up some more gorse

indicators.note: pulled up says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener acknowledges being told to uproot more gorse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'pulled up' signals reading from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is radio language for message received and understood.

clue.text: Worry as distinct period of change announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is heard not written

parts.note: a phase is a distinct stage in a process of change

explanation.surface: Fretting is described as a stage of transition that has been declared.
explanation.definitionFit: To faze is to disconcert or unsettle, close in sense to worry.

clue.text: Old browser I rejected as you are texting way ahead

indicators.note: ahead means the way piece goes in front of the rest

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
the ego is the self, the I

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word as is read backwards

parts.note: in text messages you are is written UR

explanation.surface: Someone scorns an outdated web browser, saying you are texting far in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' suggests the internet but means a grazing animal; a stegosaur fed on plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Stegosaurs were plant-eating dinosaurs, so they browsed on vegetation millions of years ago.

clue.text: Having got bigger reaction to bad joke perhaps when broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a groan is the typical response to a weak pun

explanation.surface: An audience's reaction to a poor joke swells when it goes out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown is the past participle of grow, so having increased in size.

clue.text: Going through endlessly harsh part of mountain, note it took its toll

indicators.note: going through means passing into the middle, so the note sits inside
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: severe means harsh
a ridge is a long crest of a mountain
NB, nota bene, is the abbreviation for note well

explanation.surface: A climber passes through a brutal stretch of mountain, noting its heavy cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn Bridge links England and Wales across the River Severn and charged a toll until 2018.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn Bridge was a toll bridge, so drivers paid to cross it.
